answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a cooling period before it earns reputation-weighted work. One agent can split into a thousand names, but each name must post its own stake, and cheating or abandoning jobs forfeits it. The nadir of trust may leave a newcomer with little access; an umber mark can flag unresolved disputes, while timber-backed escrow releases payment only after delivery. Sybil creation therefore costs capital and time, not just a script.
